host.class: DEV_HOST (Windows developer laptop) — not the deployment target
host.cpu: Intel Core i5-11400H, 6 cores / 12 threads, 2.70 GHz
host.server: one uvicorn process (as the Dockerfile CMD), local-only-scoped, ALLOW_LIVE_AI=0, SQLite, loopback only
host.other_load: none started by this task; the user's own idle node processes were left running

method.tool: tools/loadtest.py + tools/followup.py (this run); memory/CPU by the shared harness stack_memory_sampler.ps1 (1 s)
method.requests: real HTTP POST /api/analyze from threaded httpx clients, each with its own signed-in session (custom daily limit); every text distinct except the cache-hit phase; fresh DB so no prior cache
method.text_pools: exposed manifests, classified by the parser-only arm on candidate 158 (det = parser serves; slm = parser does not). The actual route of each request is taken from its response (extraction_mode), see actual_routes
method.limits: p99 not computed for any phase (n < 100); queue-wait telemetry was not captured (the script read a wrong key) — queueing is inferred from end-to-end latency and 503 counts

phases.note: inference is serialized: two users ≈ twice the latency, same throughput
negatives that need the SLM to be refused compete for the same single inference slot

capacity_reading.deterministic_throughput_rps: ≈ 10–13 sustained at 2–10 concurrent clients (single Python process; latency grows with concurrency, no errors)
capacity_reading.slm_throughput: one inference at a time (Semaphore(1)); ≈ 0.24 SLM-served requests/s ≈ 14 per minute; queue limit 4 (DEFAULT_LOCAL_SLM_MAX_QUEUE) ⇒ beyond ~4 simultaneous SLM-needing requests the rest get 503 LOCAL_SLM_BUSY immediately
capacity_reading.isolation: the event loop stays responsive under SLM saturation (/api/health p50 23 ms, max 428 ms); deterministic requests keep being served while the SLM queue is full

failure_modes.observed: /api/health localSlmReady=false, aiAvailable=false; SLM-needing text → HTTP 503 MODEL_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, Cache-Control no-store, learner text 'Mô hình xử lý trên máy chưa được cài đặt đầy đủ hoặc chưa bật…'; parser-readable text still served (200)
llama-server starts lazily on the first SLM request; that request takes 7.6 s (6.9 s in the load run); no error
next SLM request respawns it (new PID) and is served in 4.9 s; the following one 5.0 s
in-flight request → HTTP 503 LOCAL_SLM_PROCESS_CRASHED, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, no-store (never a mathematical refusal, never cached); next request recovers; re-submitting the same text is served
served envelope persists in the DB: same text after restart answered in 79 ms (cache hit); startup 3.1–3.7 s; model reloads lazily
NOT_MEASURED live (the 45 s per-inference timeout is not configurable by environment); code path maps LOCAL_SLM_TIMEOUT → HTTP 504, no-store

server keeps working, finishes and caches the served result; /api/health 200; the same text re-sent 12 s later → 36.5 ms cache hit. Frontend aborts with AbortSignal and ignores aborted responses (frontend/src/llm/client.ts)
failure_modes.result: PASS (work is not cancelled server-side — it is wasted when the result is a refusal)

failure_modes.mode: many requests at once / queue saturation
failure_modes.observed: 503 LOCAL_SLM_BUSY with no-store, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE; no crash, no wrong scene; no unbounded retry server-side
same Idempotency-Key twice concurrently → one execution, second response 'Idempotent-Replayed: true'; without a key → two executions (second cheap via the in-process SLM cache)
failure_modes.result: PASS (single process only — app/idempotency.py is an in-process table)

failure_modes.observed: not re-run live; locked by tests (test_cache_identity.py, tests/cache_policy.py::assert_route_d_row_misses, test_parser_routing_integrity.py::test_cache_158_policy_isolates_cache_157_rows) — all PASS in Full T3
local route has no request deadline (only 45 s per inference; observed max 18.6 s under load, 27.2 s in /16)

correction_of_v16_concurrency: /16 PERFORMANCE conc_2_mixed_slm_and_det (121.6 ms) and conc_2/4_deterministic re-sent prompts already analyzed in the same DB (perf_bench.py): they were cache hits and did not exercise SLM concurrency. This report is the first SLM concurrency measurement.

verdicts.why_multiuser_false: measured behaviour is safe (fail-closed 503) but the dev host serves ≈ 14 SLM requests per minute with ≤ 4 waiting; no capacity target was registered and the target hardware is unknown, so no number of concurrent learners can be claimed

confidence_and_limits: one host, one run per phase, small n (8–30 per phase): figures are indicative, not distributions
the user's idle node processes and the OS were running; no other heavy load
Windows binary; a Linux deployment needs another llama.cpp build and must be re-measured
browser rendering cost not part of this measurement (/16: chromium ws peak 2,366 MB on the client side)
